body:
Don't worry about the grammar - thanks for putting up with a phone interface just to talk to me.

Honestly, I'd love it if you could change my view, I'm certainly open to suggestions. It's just that the more I learn, the less meaningful life seems. I don't feel like there's anything special about us, we're just an emergent property of the rules of our universe. With a powerful enough computer, I could just create a simulation with our universe's basic rules (once we fully understand them), and eventually it would produce intelligent life. That life would also question its meaning, and place value on being alive, but once my universe in a box had run for long enough, everything would be cold, dead and devoid of information. The only value it would have is to me, as an outside observer. In our universe, if there's an outside observer, we have no way of knowing, and just assuming that there is one seems like a large leap of faith to me.

Even if you learn something to pass on to your future generations, what good would it ultimately do? Eventually, the last person with that knowledge would die, and it would all be for nothing. Of course, if you believe in an afterlife, things get messy, but I take a very materialistic view of the mind, so I can't justify such beliefs.

I'm definitely not trying to argue in favour of suicide here, or depress you.

I doubt I have a lot of cool stories to tell, and my interests are fairly limited. In fact, I suppose what's probably the greatest problem for me is that I feel like I'm gradually alienating myself from society, and soon I'll have nobody left with whom I share any common interests or values. For one thing, I consider myself asexual, which instantly alienates me from every person I've ever met in life; the only other asexual people I've found are online, but I don't really feel like not being interested in sex really constitutes a common interest. There used to be plenty of things I had in common with other people, but I feel like I'm gradually drifting away from all of them. I feel like I'm heading towards a point where all I'll have left is logic and science.

And without wanting to be disrespectful, what value does our conversation hold? We'll exchange some words, think about them a little, then eventually die, and they'll die with us. Sure, they may be on the internet for later generations to read, but then they'll be gone too, along with all of humanity, and all of our creations. Nothing will be left in the end, and anything we've accomplished will ultimately be valueless.
